title: Chat clients and the agent pipeline
summary: Every agent run flows through layers: agent middleware, a context layer (history and context providers), then a chat client with its own decorators. Knowing the layer tells you where an extension belongs.
useIf: You are deciding where to put a guardrail, memory, logging or retry, or swapping a model provider.
avoidIf: You only call an agent with default settings and no extension points.

explain.md: A **chat client** talks to a model service: Foundry, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama and others [[tr1]]. A `ChatClientAgent` (.NET, over any `IChatClient`) or `Agent` (Python, over any client implementing `SupportsChatGetResponse`) wraps it. Direct agent types wrap a managed or remote runtime instead: `FoundryAgent`, `A2AAgent`, `GitHubCopilotAgent`, `ClaudeAgent` [[tr52]]. Semantic Kernel's `ChatCompletionAgent`, `OpenAIAssistantAgent` and `AzureAIAgent` collapse into `ChatClientAgent` [[tr39]].

**Three layers in .NET**: agent middleware (added with `.Use()`), the context layer (`ChatHistoryProvider` and `AIContextProviders`), then the chat client with decorators. In **Python** the outer `Agent` is `AgentMiddlewareLayer` plus `AgentTelemetryLayer` around `RawAgent`, which runs one `context_providers` list. The inner, interchangeable ChatClient runs `FunctionInvocation` (the tool loop, with function middleware and telemetry per tool call), then chat middleware and telemetry per model call, then the provider-specific `RawChatClient` [[tr3]].

explain.title: One run through the Python pipeline
explain.alt: Request passes agent middleware, context providers, the function invocation loop and chat middleware before reaching the model; the response returns through the same layers.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  U[Caller] --> AM[Agent middleware and telemetry]
  AM --> CP[Context providers: history and memory]
  CP --> FI[Function invocation loop]
  FI --> CM[Chat middleware per model call]
  CM --> M[(Model service)]
  FI -.->|per tool call| FM[Function middleware]

blocks.code:
IChatClient chat = projectClient.GetProjectOpenAIClient()
    .GetProjectResponsesClient()
    .AsIChatClient(deployment)
    .AsBuilder()
    .Use(getResponseFunc: LogModelCalls, getStreamingResponseFunc: null)
    .Build();

AIAgent agent = new ChatClientAgent(chat, instructions: "You are helpful.")
    .AsBuilder()
    .Use(runFunc: GuardRun, runStreamingFunc: GuardRunStreaming)
    .Build();

agent = Agent(
    client=FoundryChatClient(credential=cred, project_endpoint=ep, model=model),
    instructions='You are helpful.',
    middleware=[guard_run, audit_tool_calls, log_model_calls],
    context_providers=[InMemoryHistoryProvider('memory', load_messages=True)],
)

explain.title: Chat middleware runs per model call
explain.md: Since 1.0.0rc5 (2026-03-19) chat middleware runs for every model call, including each tool-loop iteration, not once per run. Code that assumed one call per run can act twice [[tr4]].

whereToUse: Adding a guardrail once for every agent type, including remote agents, with agent middleware
Switching from Azure OpenAI to Foundry or another provider by replacing only the chat client
Cross-cutting concerns: timing, audit, retries and redaction at the right layer
Debugging: reading the order of layers to explain why a hook fired twice or not at all

use: Put policy that applies to the whole run at the agent layer
Put model-call concerns (token logging, request rewriting) at the chat layer
Put memory and history at the context layer, keyed by `source_id` in session state
avoid: Do not add chat middleware to count runs: it fires per model call
Do not assume agent-level decorators know the agent type: they must stay generic
Do not skip the default function wrapping in .NET (`UseProvidedChatClientAsIs = true`) unless you supply your own tool loop
flips: You need to see raw prompts sent to the provider: use chat middleware, not agent middleware
The agent is remote (`A2AAgent`): only agent-level decorators apply, because there is no local chat client

pitfalls.symptom: A rate-limit or audit hook fires several times per user message
pitfalls.cause: Chat middleware runs for each model call, and a tool loop makes several
pitfalls.fix: Move run-level logic to agent middleware, keep chat middleware idempotent

pitfalls.symptom: Middleware added to a decorated agent never runs for streaming calls (.NET)
pitfalls.cause: Only `runFunc` was supplied, so streaming runs through the non-streaming path

scenarios.title: Mask card numbers before the model sees them
scenarios.situation: A support assistant must redact card numbers from user messages and tool results before any model call. It uses tools that return customer records.
constraints: Redaction must cover tool results re-sent to the model
Mixed agent types in the fleet
unknowns: Is redaction needed in stored history too?
Do remote agents (A2A) need the same rule?
Is a regex enough or is an ML detector needed?
scenarios.question: Where do you put the redaction?

options.name: Chat middleware, which sees every message list sent to the model including tool results
options.why: It runs per model call, so tool results in later iterations are covered too.
options.tradeoff: Runs on every call (cost grows with tool iterations) and does not change what history storage keeps.

options.name: Agent middleware on the user input only
options.why: Tool results enter later in the loop and bypass it.
options.tradeoff: Right for input-only rules, such as blocking a banned topic before the run starts.

options.name: A context provider that rewrites history after the run
options.tradeoff: Too late for the in-flight model call that already saw the numbers.

flips.if: Stored transcripts must also be clean
flips.then: Add a history-side filter in addition to chat middleware.

flips.if: The fleet includes remote A2A agents
flips.then: Apply the rule inside each remote agent too, because your chat layer is not in their path.

scenarios.takeaway: Pick the layer by what the hook must see: the run, the model call or the tool call.

scenarios.title: Swap the model provider
scenarios.situation: A team wants to move an agent from Azure OpenAI to Foundry and later test another model family. Conversations are stored in your own database.
constraints: Tools and instructions must stay unchanged
unknowns: Is any history stored service-side with `resp_*` ids?
Do prompts depend on provider-specific options?
scenarios.question: How do you structure the swap?

options.name: Keep the agent and providers, replace only the chat client behind it
options.why: The client is the interchangeable inner component. Caller-managed history ports across providers.
options.tradeoff: Provider-specific options and tool behaviour still need a regression run.

options.name: Rewrite the agent for each provider
options.tradeoff: Only justified when a provider needs a wholly different runtime, such as a managed `FoundryAgent`.

options.name: Use service-managed history on both and copy ids
options.why: Ids such as `resp_*` are scoped to a key or project and are not portable across providers.
options.tradeoff: Works only inside one provider and project.

flips.if: You must switch models mid-conversation in .NET
flips.then: Look at the experimental `RoutePersistingRoutingChatClient` (Python and Go have no equivalent) [[tr47]].

flips.if: A managed runtime such as `FoundryAgent` must own the conversation
flips.then: History becomes service-managed, so compaction does not apply and model switching needs a new conversation.

scenarios.takeaway: Caller-managed history plus a swappable client keeps provider choice cheap.

quiz.q: Order the Python pipeline for one run, outermost first.
quiz.explain: The agent layer wraps the run, RawAgent runs context providers, then the ChatClient tool loop calls chat middleware for each model call before the provider client.

quiz.q: A logging hook registered as chat middleware writes five lines for one user question that triggered four tool calls. Why?
options: The agent is retried five times
The session was serialized five times
The hook is registered at run level
Chat middleware runs for each model call and the tool loop made several
quiz.explain: Chat middleware runs inside the function invocation loop, once per model call. Retries, run-level registration and serialization do not cause it.

flashcards.back: Agent middleware (`.Use()`), the context layer (`ChatHistoryProvider` plus `AIContextProviders`), and the chat client (`IChatClient` with decorators).

flashcards.front: How often does Python chat middleware run?
flashcards.back: On every model call, including each tool-loop iteration (since 1.0.0rc5, 2026-03-19).

flashcards.front: Which layer works with any agent type, including `A2AAgent`?
flashcards.back: Agent middleware, because it wraps the whole run and makes no assumption about the inner agent.
